name: BitPoint
rootCause: On July 12, Japan's BitPoint Japan (BPJ) exchange was hacked, and 3.5 billion yen (32 million U.S. dollars) worth of cryptocurrency in the hot wallet was stolen. After that, BPJ shut down all services of the exchange. On the 14th, BPJ announced the recovery of some stolen cryptocurrencies from overseas trading systems, reducing the total loss to 3.02 billion yen (customer funds 2.06 billion, BPJ own funds 960 million).

descriptions.text: On July 12, Japan's BitPoint Japan (BPJ) exchange was hacked, and 3.5 billion yen (32 million U.S. dollars) worth of cryptocurrency in the hot wallet was stolen. After that, BPJ shut down all services of the exchange. On the 14th, BPJ announced the recovery of some stolen cryptocurrencies from overseas trading systems, reducing the total loss to 3.02 billion yen (customer funds 2.06 billion, BPJ own funds 960 million).

BITPoint disclosed a July 2019 hot-wallet breach after an XRP remittance anomaly exposed unauthorized withdrawals from BTC, BCH, ETH, LTC, and XRP custody. Public disclosures revised the loss to about ¥3.028 billion, but the entry path into the wallet environment was not established. Unauthorized withdrawals were made from BITPoint's hot-wallet environment. The public record does not establish how the attacker obtained access to that environment or which control failed first.
